note: Subprocess APIs WITHOUT a shell. The exploit class is argument injection: a value that becomes argv[0], a leading '-' flag, or a subcommand — not metacharacters. Rev 1 buried this in one EXEC row.

sinks.name: Runtime.exec(String)
gates: whitespace-tokenized, no shell: inject arguments, not metachars

sinks.name: Process.Start
gates: UseShellExecute=false is the modern default — no shell

sinks.name: os/exec.Cmd
gates: no shell unless the command is explicitly sh -c

sinks.name: subprocess.run/Popen([...]) argv form
gates: metachars are literal; leading '-' becomes a flag

verified.what: argv form prints '&&' literally; no shell interpretation

sinks.name: proc_open(array cmd, ...)
gates: array form bypasses the shell — the oft-missed inverse of proc_open(string)

verified.what: proc_open array args: '; rm -rf' stays literal

hazards: argument injection survives correct quoting — look for attacker values that become a flag ('-o', '--upload-pack', '-K') or argv[0]
tool delegates (git, curl, ssh, ImageMagick) parse the injected flag themselves
non_transfers: pure metachar payloads — dead on this family
